To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most frequent copy number alterations in human prostate cancer are deletions of chromosome arms 8p, 10q and 13q and gains of chromosome arms 7p, 8q, 12p, 17q and 20q.

(i) the most frequent copy number changes in prostate cancer are gains at 8q, losses at 8p, and losses at 8 p, 10 q, 13 q, and X q; (ii) gains at 7p, 7 q, and 17 q are associated with more aggressive disease; and (iii) losses at 8, 10, and 16 are associated with less aggressive disease.

DNA copy number alterations occur in 8q, 8p, 17p, 13q, 16q, 10q, 18q, 7p, 9p, 10p, and 16p in prostate cancer, and that 8p, the most frequently altered chromosomal region, contains a number of candidate prostate cancer genes, including the well-known tumor suppressor gene NKX3.1.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most common regions of deletion in prostate cancers include the 8p, 10p, 13q, 16q, and Xq regions, while the most common regions gained in prostate cancers are the 7p, 8q, 12q, 17q, and 20q regions.
the most common DNA copy number losses are on chromosomes 8p, 10, 13, 16q, and 17, and the most common DNA gains are on chromosomes 7 and 8q.
the most common DNA copy number alteration in prostate cancer is the loss of 8p, followed by 13q and 10q.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there are a number of common regions that are frequently altered in prostate cancer, including gains of 8p12-p21.3, 8q24.1, 7q21.1-q22.1, 1q12-q25 and 17q21-q24 and losses of 16q23-q24, 10q25-q26, 8p21.3-p22, 8p23.3-p11.23, 8p11.
there are at least 10 regions that are commonly gained in prostate cancers.
the 8p21.3-p21.1 region was the most frequently deleted region in prostate cancers, while 8q24 was the most frequently gained region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most common copy number alteration is deletion on chromosome arm 8p (8p deletion).
the most common DNA copy number changes in prostate cancer are losses of chromosomes 8p, 13q, 16q and 18q, and gains of chromosomes 1q, 7, 8q and 17q.
there are several common regions of DNA copy number alterations that are shared across all studies and tumor types.
